newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Suspect in Sri Lanka lawmaker killing surrenders.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Sri Lanka lawmaker killing surrenders.

text.p: The key suspect in the killing of a Sri Lankan legislator surrendered to a Colombo judge on Thursday after nine days of hiding from police, an official at the Colombo Fort magistrate's court said.

Susantha Punchinilame, a main opposition United National Party (UNP) lawmaker, turned himself in to acting magistrate Jayantha Dias Nanayakkara of the central Colombo Fort area, said the official, who declined to be identified.

A senior official at the police criminal investigation unit confirmed the surrender. He said Punchinilame would be remanded before being presented before the magistrate of the southern town of Ratnapura, where the killing took place last week.
He did no say when Punchinilame would be presented in court.
Another key suspect in the killing of ruling People's Alliance coalition lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala, the former UNP mayor of Ratnapura Mahinda Ratnatilleke, surrendered to a Colombo judge on Sunday.
Police had offered a one-million-rupee ($17,500) reward for information leading to the arrest of either Punchinilame or Ratnatilleke.
Ellalwala, the youngest member of Sri Lanka's 225-seat parliament, was gunned down during a roadside quarrel between supporters of the alliance and supporters of the rival UNP.
His killing sparked two days of riots in Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) from Colombo as pro-alliance activists set fire to buildings and houses owned by UNP supporters.
